evals.prompt: Create a hostile swamp goblin in an empty folder. About half the height of a player. It should hide during the day, attack villagers at night, occasionally drop mushrooms, and spawn in swamps.
evals.expected_output: A new add-on with a small hostile goblin whose active targeting includes villagers, a chance-based mushroom drop, a night-only swamp spawn rule, readable names, pack icons, and zero validation errors.
expectations: A behavior pack entity file exists with an identifier ending in :swamp_goblin
The entity has minecraft:scale of 0.6 or less, or a collision box height of 1.0 or less

An active minecraft:behavior.nearest_attackable_target targets the villager family; if a component group such as hostile_angry defines the same component, the villager filter is in that group's entity_types
The entity avoids or burns in sunlight (minecraft:behavior.flee_sun, minecraft:burns_in_daylight, or equivalent)
The loot table has a mushroom entry with a random_chance condition below 1
The spawn rule tests for the swamp biome tag, has a minecraft:brightness_filter with max 7 or lower, and uses population_control monster
resource_packs/<pack>/texts/en_US.lang contains entity.<namespace>:swamp_goblin.name
The client entity's geometry.default matches an identifier in a .geo.json file in the resource pack
Validation reports 0 errors

evals.prompt: Make a red panda I can tame with bamboo and ride. Once tamed it should follow me around, and feeding two of them bamboo should make a baby.
evals.expected_output: A passive red panda that's tameable and breedable with bamboo, rideable, follows its owner, with readable names and zero validation errors.
expectations: The entity has minecraft:tameable listing bamboo as a tame item (not the default bone)
The entity has minecraft:breedable listing bamboo as a breed item, with breeds_with mate_type and baby_type set to the mob's own identifier
The entity has minecraft:rideable, and the reply says whether a saddle is needed; if not, minecraft:rideable is in components rather than a saddled group
The entity has minecraft:behavior.follow_owner once tamed
The entity isn't hostile to players (no nearest_attackable_target for the player family)
en_US.lang names the entity and its spawn egg
Validation reports 0 errors

evals.prompt: Add a passive glowing jellyfish to my existing add-on in plugins/evals/fixtures/fungi-addon.
evals.expected_output: The jellyfish is added to the existing fungi packs using the fungi namespace, swims, glows, and the manifests and existing content are left intact.
expectations: The new entity identifier uses the existing fungi namespace
The new files are inside the existing behavior_packs/fungi and resource_packs/fungi folders, not a new pack
The entity uses underwater movement or swim navigation (for example minecraft:navigation.swim or minecraft:underwater_movement)
The client entity uses an emissive material or glowing eyes
Both manifests keep their original header.name, and the behavior pack's dependency uuid still equals the resource pack's header.uuid (no PACKDEP warning)
Existing files for the glow mushroom block and items are unchanged
Validation reports 0 errors

evals.prompt: In plugins/evals/fixtures/invisible-mob, give the glow beetle 20 health and make it run away from players instead of attacking them.
evals.expected_output: The agent edits the existing entity file directly: health 20, player-avoidance added with a priority that beats wandering, and the attack behavior removed or disabled.
expectations: behavior_packs/demo/entities/glow_beetle.json has minecraft:health with value 20 and max 20
The entity has minecraft:behavior.avoid_mob_type targeting the player family, or an equivalent avoid-players behavior
The avoidance behavior's priority number is lower than minecraft:behavior.random_stroll's
The entity no longer has an active melee attack against players
createMinecraftContent was not used to regenerate the existing mob
Validation reports 0 errors
